input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: The MFN runs the wrong way: § 7.2 obliges Customer (us) to disclose and match, for Vendor's benefit, any more favourable commercial offer we receive. It is unlimited as to product, term and comparability and has no reasonable-comparison carve-outs, so it fails the fallback (MFN limited to a defined product, 12 months, with carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory (open-ended obligation to extend Vendor any better third-party terms). It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Smallest fix reaching the preferred position is deletion of the obligation; no Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document that would be lost.

proposal.summary: Delete Customer's obligation to disclose and match more favourable third-party offers for Vendor
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted § 7.2 because it imposes an open-ended most-favoured-nation and match obligation on us, which our playbook does not accept and which contradicts § 12.3's confirmation that we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.
